idiom_name: pthread worker pool + per-worker work-stealing deque (C11 atomics)
implementation_notes: C has no task abstraction, so the classic realization is hand-written: a fixed pool of pthreads, one double-ended queue per worker, and a recursive split function that pushes child tasks onto the local deque (push/pop at one end) while idle workers steal from the opposite end. Use C11 <stdatomic.h> for the deque indices and pthread_mutex/pthread_cond only for the pool's sleep path; the join is a per-task completion flag that a waiting worker must keep polling while it continues to run or steal other tasks. OpenMP's task/taskgroup constructs are the runtime-provided alternative - the runtime owns the pool, the queues and the stealing - so prefer them whenever the toolchain supports OpenMP.
pitfalls: A worker that blocks in pthread_cond_wait at a join stops stealing; joins must poll or help while waiting or the pool can deadlock.
The deque needs single-owner push/pop with a one-thief take path; guarding the whole deque with a single mutex serializes the hot path.
pthread_create per task is not fork/join: thread creation costs orders of magnitude more than the task it runs, so tasks must be pool-local structs.

variants.name: OpenMP task/taskgroup runtime
variants.idiom_name: #pragma omp task / taskgroup inside a parallel region
variants.implementation_notes: OpenMP 3.0 added tasks precisely for irregular and recursive parallelism: the fork-join team comes from #pragma omp parallel, #pragma omp task generates child tasks, and #pragma omp taskgroup waits for the child tasks of the current task and all their descendants (the join). The runtime's own queues schedule the tasks, so a blockaded leaf does not need hand-written deques. The decomposition stays yours; data-sharing clauses are where correctness lives - variables are shared by default, so leaf results must use reduction/task_reduction or be captured per task.
pitfalls: Variables are shared by default: results merged from child tasks need reduction/task_reduction (or firstprivate captures) or the leaves race.
Omitting the enclosing taskgroup lets the parent run past the fork - results are read before the children produced them.
Nested parallel regions oversubscribe unless nesting is disabled; task granularity still matters because every #pragma omp task carries runtime overhead.
